categories.name: ESP32-C3 Platform & Power
categories.description: Covers the selected development board and the system power-input hardware requirements.
requirements: The microcontroller unit shall be an ESP32-C3 development board.
The system power input shall be 5 V supplied via micro‑USB from a 12 V automotive adapter.

categories.name: DHT22 Climate Sensing
categories.description: Covers DHT22 selection, GPIO power and signal wiring, periodic temperature and humidity acquisition, and sample validation behavior.
requirements: The firmware shall read temperature from the DHT22 every 2000 ms.
The firmware shall read humidity from the DHT22 every 2000 ms.

For each DHT22 sample, the firmware shall verify the sensor checksum; on checksum failure it shall retry once within the same 2000 ms cycle and, if still invalid, shall not update the published temperature/humidity for that cycle.
The DHT22 data output shall be connected to ESP32-C3 GPIO2.
The DHT22 VCC pin shall be connected to 3.3 V.
The DHT22 GND pin shall be connected to ground.
The climate sensor shall be a DHT22 providing temperature and humidity.

categories.name: MPU6050 Motion Sensing & I2C Driver
categories.description: Covers MPU6050 hardware and I2C wiring, startup validation and configuration, acceleration acquisition, unit conversion, and vehicle-axis mapping.
requirements: The firmware shall read X, Y, and Z acceleration from the MPU6050.
The firmware shall convert the MPU6050 acceleration readings to G-force units for output.
The firmware shall map IMU axes such that X corresponds to lateral (cornering), Y to longitudinal (acceleration/braking), and Z to vertical (bumps).

At startup, the firmware shall verify MPU6050 presence via its identity register and initialize it to a defined measurement range and filtering configuration so acceleration‑to‑g conversion is deterministic.
The MPU6050 SCL pin shall be connected to ESP32-C3 GPIO8.
The MPU6050 SDA pin shall be connected to ESP32-C3 GPIO9.
The MPU6050 VCC pin shall be connected to 3.3 V.
The MPU6050 GND pin shall be connected to ground.
The inertial measurement unit shall be an MPU6050 3-axis accelerometer.

categories.name: WiFi & MQTT Communication
categories.description: Covers WiFi provisioning and reconnection, MQTT broker configuration and recovery, telemetry and alert publishing, message schemas and topics, timing, bounded queueing, and non-blocking communication behavior.
requirements: The system shall monitor interior cabin climate and vehicle ride dynamics using the ESP32-C3 and shall publish the data over MQTT.
The firmware shall connect to WiFi automatically on startup.
The firmware shall reconnect to WiFi if the connection drops.
The firmware shall publish climate and motion data as a single JSON payload to MQTT every 2000 ms.
The firmware shall persist the WiFi SSID and password in non‑volatile storage so the device can connect automatically on startup without user interaction.
The firmware shall detect MQTT broker disconnection and automatically reconnect and resume periodic and alert publications without user intervention.
The device shall use WiFi SSID "GopalaSutharsan" for network association.
The device shall use the WiFi password "123987456" to authenticate to the specified SSID.
Each periodic telemetry JSON message shall include the keys: temp_c, humidity_percent, lateral_g, longitudinal_g, and vertical_g.
Alert messages shall be published to the MQTT topic "vehicle/cabin/alert" on a threshold event.
Each alert JSON message shall include temp_c, humidity_percent, lateral_g, longitudinal_g, vertical_g, and a field "trigger" indicating which metric triggered the alert.
The firmware shall provide a configurable MQTT broker hostname/IP and TCP port used for publishing telemetry and alerts.
Each periodic telemetry message shall be published on MQTT topic "vehicle/cabin/telemetry" at 2000 ms intervals.

MQTT publish operations shall use a finite timeout and shall not block the 2000 ms sensor sampling schedule; if a publish cannot complete within the timeout, the attempt shall be aborted and normal sampling shall continue.
WiFi connection and reconnection attempts shall use finite timeouts and a backoff strategy and shall not block sensor acquisition or alert evaluation.
Any internal queueing of MQTT messages shall be bounded to prevent RAM exhaustion; when the bound is reached, the oldest unsent telemetry shall be discarded in favor of newer data.

categories.name: Alert Threshold Configuration & Evaluation
categories.description: Covers configurable climate and G-force thresholds, immediate alert evaluation and publication triggers, and atomic non-volatile persistence of threshold values.
requirements: The firmware shall maintain a configurable alert threshold for temperature.
The firmware shall maintain a configurable alert threshold for humidity.
The firmware shall maintain a configurable alert threshold for G-force.
The firmware shall publish immediately to the alert topic when any configured threshold is exceeded, independent of the regular 2000 ms cycle.
Updates to configurable alert thresholds shall be stored atomically in non‑volatile memory and shall persist across power cycles; after reset the most recently committed values shall be in effect.

categories.name: Diagnostics, Security & Fault Recovery
categories.description: Covers boot and on-demand serial diagnostics, credential redaction, sensor and publish health counters, watchdog and brown-out recovery, and post-reset service resumption.
requirements: The firmware shall enable a watchdog mechanism and, upon watchdog expiration or brown‑out reset, shall automatically reboot and resume WiFi association and MQTT telemetry without user action.

On boot, the firmware shall output a single‑line status over the serial console including: firmware version, configured SSID, MQTT broker endpoint, and sensor initialization results; credentials shall be redacted.
The firmware shall maintain counters of sensor read failures per sensor and MQTT publish failures and shall make them available via the serial console on request.
The firmware shall not include WiFi or MQTT credentials in telemetry payloads or console logs and shall redact them in any status output.
